threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘the Overground’ instead of ‘the G’, and you have no clue about secret bus routes. Good luck figuring out the night tube schedule!
Last night on the 59, saw a guy in a full tuxedo serenading a group of drunk friends. Only in Brixton would you find an impromptu opera on a night bus.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw a mom juggling a toddler, a dog, and a grocery bag while chatting on her phone, all without breaking a sweat. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how Kreuzberg's street vendors sell currywurst at 3 AM, while other cities are closing up shop? It's a late-night salvation.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission if they can name at least five taco trucks that aren’t on food apps but still serve fire burritos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The other day, a saxophonist serenaded a bus full of commuters stuck at the Civic Center. Only in SF do the delays come with a soundtrack.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists love to grab their ‘totally local’ coffee in Gràcia, but most don’t realize it’s the locals who prefer the hidden corner bars over the trendy spots.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily; they’re the ones still trying to pronounce 'Eixample' correctly while juggling a map and a gelato.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘the tube’ instead of just taking the Overground like a local. The awks when you’re stood there waiting for a train.
Last week on the 59, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with 90s R&B. Half the passengers were singing along, completely ignoring the driver.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a wedding procession using the BVG bus as their float, everyone just cheering and clapping, that was Neukölln for me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous dance parties in the U-Bahn stations here. Just the other week at Samariterstraße, a crowd gathered for a surprise rave!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows the taco truck on 24th hits different after a night out, while the tourists pile into the overpriced burrito joints.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo exit the 31-Philosopher, adjust his tie, and stroll right into the opera house. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think the best tapas are in the fancy spots, but it's the tiny bars with locals that have the real deal. Less flash, more flavor.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones fumbling with the metro map at Girona station while locals breeze by, smartphones in hand. So eager to explore, yet still lost in translation.
